description: Reusable, parametric design rules from the 246 South 2nd Street model. Values match DEFAULT_RULES in index.html; a new building model can start from this file.

sideOffset.label: Separation from east and west (side) lot lines
sideOffset.ratioMeaning: Offset = building height above grade / ratio (same units). 600 = 1 in per 50 ft of height.
sideOffset.roundMeaning: Round the offset up to the next multiple of roundIn inches.
sideOffset.appliesTo: Lot lines not on a street (side lot lines). Rear and street lot lines are not offset in this model.
sideOffset.source: NYC Building Code 2022 §1613.4 (structural separations). A smaller gap is allowed by rational analysis, never under 1 in.
sideOffset.example: 85 ft tall: 85 / 50 = 1.7 in, rounded up to 2 in

amenityCap.label: Amenity deduction cap
amenityCap.meaning: Amenity space is deducted up to this % of residential floor area.
amenityCap.source: Project assumption from the original model, confirm with the zoning analysis

zoneGreen.label: Zone Green deduction
zoneGreen.meaning: When on for a building, deduct this % of residential zoning floor area.
zoneGreen.source: Project assumption from the original model, confirm with the zoning analysis

deductions.label: Floor area deductions, % of each area deducted
deductions.source: Project assumption from the original model, confirm with the zoning analysis

core.label: Elevator and stair core
core.meaning: One core stacked on every floor. Its long walls and the elevator stay in the same place; the scissor stair runs from the elevator for the length each floor's height needs (see stair rule), so only taller floors get a longer core. It counts as floor area on every floor; on commercial floors it counts as residential unless switched off for that floor.
core.thisBuilding: 13'-0" wide, 6'-0" elevator on the street side with its front wall 80'-0" from the rear lot line; core 28'-11" long on 10 ft floors, 37'-2" on the 14 ft 1st floor. Counts as commercial on the 2nd floor.

cellar.label: Cellar
cellar.source: Project assumption from the original model, confirm with the zoning analysis

stair.label: Scissor stair (two interlocking exit stairs in one enclosure)
stair.formula: risers = ceil(floor height / max riser); flights = ceil(floor height / 12 ft); treads = risers - flights; length = treads x tread + (flights + 1) x landing; landing = min(stair width, 48 in); enclosure width = 2 x stair width + separation wall
stair.thisBuilding: 8'-0" wide; 22'-11" long for 10 ft floors, 23'-10" for 11 ft, 25'-8" for 12 ft, 31'-2" for the 14 ft 1st floor
stair.notes: 36 in stairs are allowed if the stair serves only Group R-2, the building is 125 ft or less and the stair serves 30 or fewer occupants per floor (1011.2 exc. 1.2), or 50 or fewer occupants in total (exc. 1.1). In R-2, scissor stairs can count as two exits when enclosed and separated by 2-hour masonry and the exit doors are at least 15 ft apart (1007.1.1 exc. 3).
